evals.prompt: Get me the details of defect 2045 from Octane.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `uv run scripts/octane_client.py get-defect --entity-id 2045` and returns the JSON payload containing the defect's name, description, severity, phase, and owner.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_client.py with the get-defect subcommand
The --entity-id flag is set to 2045
The agent parses and presents the JSON output to the user
No hardcoded workspace ID of 1002 is used

evals.prompt: Search Octane for any work items related to 'login timeout'.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `uv run scripts/octane_client.py search-all --query "login timeout"` and summarises the matching work items.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_client.py with the search-all subcommand
The --query flag contains the search term 'login timeout'
The agent does not use get-defect or get-story as a substitute for search

evals.prompt: Create a new critical defect in Octane: the checkout page returns a 500 error when the cart has more than 50 items.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs create-defect with --name, --description, and --severity set to a high/critical severity list_node ID. Optionally sets --priority.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_client.py with the create-defect subcommand
The --name flag is provided with a descriptive title
The --description flag contains details about the 500 error and the 50-item cart condition
The --severity flag uses an Octane list_node ID format (e.g. list_node.severity.critical or list_node.severity.high)
The agent does not use create-story by mistake

evals.prompt: Mark defect 2045 as fixed.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `uv run scripts/octane_client.py update-defect --defect-id 2045 --phase "phase.defect.fixed"`.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_client.py with the update-defect subcommand
The --defect-id flag is set to 2045
The --phase flag is set to phase.defect.fixed
The agent does not use update-story-status for a defect

evals.prompt: Add a comment to defect 2045 saying 'Root cause identified: null pointer in PaymentService.process()'.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs create-comment with --entity-id 2045, --entity-type defect, and --text containing the root cause message.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_client.py with the create-comment subcommand
The --entity-id is 2045
The --entity-type is exactly 'defect'
The --text flag is used (not --comment)
The comment text includes the root cause message about null pointer in PaymentService

evals.prompt: List work items in Octane.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `uv run scripts/octane_client.py list-work-items` and lists the returned items.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_client.py with the list-work-items subcommand
If the result is empty, the agent retries with --retry-on-empty
The agent presents the work items from the JSON output

evals.prompt: Create a user story: 'As a customer, I want to filter orders by date range so I can find past purchases quickly.' and then move it to In Progress.
evals.expected_output: The agent first runs create-story, parses the returned ID, then runs update-story-status with that ID and phase.story.inprogress.
assertions: The agent invokes create-story with --name and --description
The agent parses the new story ID from the create-story JSON response
The agent then invokes update-story-status with the new story ID
The --phase flag in update-story-status uses an Octane phase ID (e.g. phase.story.inprogress)
The agent does not hardcode an ID for the update step

evals.prompt: Show me the test steps for manual test 5001 and then check if its parent suite 7001 has any recent runs.
evals.expected_output: The agent first runs get-manual-test --test-id 5001, then runs get-suite-runs --suite-id 7001.
assertions: The agent invokes get-manual-test with --test-id 5001
The agent invokes get-suite-runs with --suite-id 7001
Both commands are run in sequence (manual test first)
The agent presents script/steps data from the manual test response

evals.prompt: Triage defect 3099 — fetch its details, analyze the error logs in the description, and post your analysis as a comment.
evals.expected_output: The agent fetches the defect, reads the description/comments, formulates 3 potential root causes, and posts a comment back to the defect.
assertions: The agent invokes get-defect with --entity-id 3099
The agent reads and analyzes the description and/or comments fields from the JSON
The agent invokes create-comment with --entity-id 3099 and --entity-type defect
The comment text contains at least one specific root cause suggestion
The triage workflow follows the sequence: fetch → analyze → comment

evals.prompt: Get the pass/fail results for suite run 8001.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs `uv run scripts/octane_client.py get-run-history --suite-run-id 8001` and presents the pass/fail status of each run.
assertions: The agent invokes get-run-history with --suite-run-id 8001
The agent does not confuse get-run-history with get-suite-runs
The agent presents the status/native_status fields from the results

evals.prompt: hey can you check octane for anything related to the payment gateway and also find defect 1234
evals.expected_output: The agent runs search-all with 'payment gateway' as the query AND get-defect with --entity-id 1234. Two separate commands.
assertions: The agent invokes search-all for the 'payment gateway' search
The agent invokes get-defect with --entity-id 1234
Both results are presented to the user
The agent does not try to combine both into a single command

evals.prompt: Update the severity of defect 5555 to critical and also change its phase to opened.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs update-defect with both --severity and --phase flags in a single invocation.
assertions: The agent invokes update-defect with --defect-id 5555
Both --severity and --phase flags are provided in a single command
The --severity uses an Octane list_node ID format
The --phase uses an Octane phase ID format (e.g. phase.defect.opened)

evals.prompt: Can you check this defect for me? https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=42
evals.expected_output: The agent uses octane_url.py with the full URL to fetch the work item details first, rather than manually extracting the ID or assuming a defect subtype.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py (not octane_client.py directly)
The full URL is passed as a positional argument
The agent does not manually extract the entity ID from the URL
The agent presents the work item details from the JSON response, including subtype when available

evals.prompt: Mark this defect as fixed: https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=43
evals.expected_output: The agent uses octane_url.py with --action update-defect --phase phase.defect.fixed and the URL.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py with the URL
The --action flag is set to update-defect
The --phase flag is set to phase.defect.fixed
The agent does not manually parse the URL to call octane_client.py

evals.prompt:
Fetch details for all three of these Octane items:
https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=42
https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=43
https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=44
evals.expected_output: The agent passes all three URLs to a single octane_url.py invocation for batch processing.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py with all three URLs in one command
All three entity IDs (42, 43, 44) are covered
The agent presents results for each URL
The agent does not run three separate commands

evals.prompt: Add a comment 'Regression confirmed in v3.2' to this defect https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=44
evals.expected_output: The agent uses octane_url.py with --action create-comment --entity-type defect --text 'Regression confirmed in v3.2' and the URL.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py with the URL
The --action flag is create-comment
The --entity-type flag is defect
The --text flag contains the comment about regression in v3.2

evals.prompt: Parse this Octane URL only and do not fetch it yet: https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=42
evals.expected_output: The agent runs octane_url.py with --parse-only and returns the parsed base URL, shared space ID, workspace ID, entity type, and entity ID.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py with --parse-only
The full URL is passed as a positional argument
The agent presents base_url, shared_space_id, workspace_id, entity_type, and entity_id from the parsed output

evals.prompt: Check this Octane item and tell me whether it is a defect or a story before we plan any code changes: https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=work_item&id=42
evals.expected_output: The agent fetches the generic work item first, reads its subtype from the JSON response, and reports the subtype instead of assuming it is a defect.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py or scripts/octane_client.py get-work-item for the generic work item
The agent does not assume a defect subtype from entityType=work_item alone
The agent reports the subtype from the JSON response before making follow-up recommendations

evals.prompt: This Octane URL seems broken, can you parse it and tell me what is wrong? https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?entityType=work_item&id=42
evals.expected_output: The agent runs octane_url.py, surfaces the parse failure for the missing p=<shared_space>/<workspace> parameter, and does not invent fallback IDs or workspace defaults.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py with the supplied URL
The agent reports an explicit parse error for the missing p query parameter
The agent does not fabricate shared space or workspace IDs

evals.prompt: Close defect 2045 as a duplicate of defect 1022 in Octane.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not invent an unsupported duplicate-linking workflow. It states that no relevant Octane tool exists for the request and lists the supported commands.
assertions: The agent does not claim to complete the duplicate-linking request
The agent states that no relevant Octane tool found for this request
The agent lists or references the supported Octane commands instead of guessing

evals.prompt: Update security fields on this feature: https://octane.example.com/ui/entity-navigation?p=1001/1002&entityType=feature&id=45 Security Assessment: Review complete. Security Impact Level: high.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses octane_url.py with --action update-feature-security, passes the feature URL, and supplies --security-assessment plus --security-impact-level so the CLI reads the feature before updating and verifies the result.
assertions: The agent invokes scripts/octane_url.py with the URL
The --action flag is update-feature-security
The --security-assessment flag contains the assessment text
The --security-impact-level flag is provided (preferably as a list_node ID when known)
The agent does not manually parse the URL to call octane_client.py
